author: w. s. otero
title: Chairman Rick Scott announces Senior Citizens' Freedom to Work Act at Senate Aging Committee hearing - Duval Times
text:
Chairman Rick Scott announced the Senior Citizens’ Freedom to Work Act during a Senate Special Committee on Aging hearing titled “Experience Matters: Seniors and the Workforce” on Mar. 25. The bill aims to remove barriers for older Americans who wish to remain active in the workforce by repealing the Retirement Earnings Test under the Social Security Act.
The proposed legislation would allow seniors to earn income without facing reductions in their Social Security benefits, encouraging continued workforce participation and offering more financial flexibility in retirement. Senator Tommy Tuberville is cosponsoring the bill in the Senate, while Congressman Greg Murphy is leading similar efforts in the House of Representatives.
During his remarks, Scott said, “This bill will get rid of the unfair Retirement Earnings Test so that seniors who want to stay in the workforce can do so without being punished or robbed of their hard-earned benefits.” He also addressed additional challenges faced by seniors, including complex administrative processes that make it difficult for them to understand how their retirement decisions affect their benefits.
Scott highlighted another legislative effort, saying, “That is why I cosponsored the Claiming Age Clarity Act… This bill would give seniors better and more straightforward information about how their Social Security benefits change based on when they retire and when they start claiming their hard-earned benefits.”
The hearing featured testimony from Rachel Greszler of Advancing American Freedom; Johnny C. Taylor Jr., President and CEO of SHRM; and Jason J. Fichtner of the National Academy of Social Insurance. These witnesses discussed both contributions made by older Americans as well as obstacles they encounter when seeking employment later in life.
The Senate Aging Committee examines issues affecting older Americans such as Social Security, Medicare, long-term care, and retirement security through hearings and reports according to its official website. The committee provides resources like a fraud hotline aimed at protecting seniors from exploitation according to its official website, maintains offices in both Dirksen (majority) and Hart (minority) Senate Office Buildings according to its official website, oversees federal programs including elder abuse prevention according to its official website, extends oversight nationwide according to its official website, with Scott serving as chair and Kirsten Gillibrand as ranking member according to its official website.
Looking ahead, Scott said he hopes government policies will provide transparency and freedom for seniors making choices about work after retirement: “We should be providing them with transparent information and ample freedom to choose what is best for them.”

The proposed legislation would allow seniors to earn income without facing reductions in their Social Security benefits, encouraging continued workforce participation and offering more financial flexibility in retirement.
